    44	## GitHub → local mapping
    45	
    46	| GitHub mechanism | Local replacement |
    47	|---|---|
    48	| PR CI (`pr-ci.yml`) on push/PR events | `local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id>` run by the PR lifecycle scripts |
    49	| Main-build actions cache (main-only save, PR restore) | Hot main cache: single-writer warmer + read-only snapshots + APFS copy-on-write clones per worktree (`build-cache.md`) |
    50	| `lake exe cache get` (Mathlib cloud cache) | Unchanged — already local |
    51	| Model-backed PR review chained on CI success | `local/bin/review.sh <pr-number>`: codex CLI with the same `.github/prompts/` review personas, invoked only from green exact-head CI statuses; one COMMENT review plus `local-review/summary` |
    52	| Auto-fix workflows (CI-fix, blueprint-fix, review-fix) | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode {ci,blueprint,review,auto}` with the same commit-prefix guards and a combined iteration cap |
    53	| `@claude`/`@codex` mention responders | `local/bin/agent.sh <id> "instruction"` — human-invoked codex session on the branch worktree |
    54	| GitHub issues + sub-issues + labels | unchanged — GitHub is the record again (`issues-prs.md`); `issue_new.py` / `issue_close.py` drive it through `gh_common.py` |
    55	| GitHub PRs | GitHub PRs, branch-per-issue, merge gate in `pr_merge.py` (REST merge with the exact-SHA guard) |
    56	| Issue automation (classify/scout/track/followups) | `local/bin/` Python ports; LLM steps optional behind `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` |
    57	| Housekeeping crons (standup, stale audit, linter sweep, README freshness) | `local/bin/housekeeping.sh <job>` on demand |
    58	| Badges + Pages site (blueprint/docs/badges components) | `local/bin/site.sh` → component store + assembled site in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/site/` |
    59	| Codex cloud env setup (`.codex/setup.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` per worktree |
    60	| Reviewer/bot identity via tokens | codex CLI sessions; `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` registry |
    61	
    62	## Core invariants (inherited from the parent workflow's post-mortems)
    63	
    64	These encode incidents the parent repo paid for; violating them re-introduces
    65	documented failure modes. Sources are cited in `local/protocols/*.md`.
    66	
    67	1. **Single cache writer.** Only the warmer writes the hot main cache; agent
    68	   worktrees consume copy-on-write clones and never write back. (GitHub's
    69	   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)
    70	2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** The gate reads the
    71	   exact-head `local-ci/*` statuses; a failed or absent CI summary blocks the
    72	   review, which then publishes nothing at all — the *absence* of a green
    73	   `local-review/summary` is the block, never a silent skip. Bot commits with prefix
    74	   `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` are not re-reviewed except the final
    75	   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.
    76	3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,
    77	   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix
    78	   kinds; sync/audit CI failures are never auto-fixed.
    79	4. **Kill-switch semantics.** `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` and
    80	   `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` disable only on the literal string `false`;
    81	   unset means enabled.
    82	5. **Trusted prompts.** Reviewer/fixer personas are read from committed `main`
    83	   (`git show main:...`), never from the branch under review.

    85	   are injected into agent prompts with sanitization (control-char strip,

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Manage a worktree's optional external .lake directory.
+#   lake-root.sh prepare <worktree> [--check]
+#   lake-root.sh cleanup <repository> <branch>
+set -euo pipefail
+log() { printf '[lake-root] %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
+die() { printf '[lake-root] ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
+run_outside_git_env() (
+  if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    for name in $(git rev-parse --local-env-vars); do
+      unset "$name" || true
+    done
+  fi
+  "$@"
+)
+canonical_lake_root() { # <create: 0|1>
+  local create="$1" root="${MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT:-}"
+  [ -n "$root" ] || return 1
+  case "$root" in
+    /*) ;;
+    *) die "MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT must be an absolute path: $root" ;;
+  esac
+  [ "$root" != "/" ] || die "MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT must not be /"
+  if [ "$create" -eq 1 ]; then
+    mkdir -p "$root"
+  else
+    [ -d "$root" ] || die "MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT does not exist: $root"
+  fi
+  (cd "$root" && pwd -P)
+}
+worktree_branch() { # <worktree>
+  local branch
+  branch="$(run_outside_git_env git -C "$1" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD 2>/dev/null)" \
+    || die "$1 is detached; MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT requires a branch-owned worktree"
+  run_outside_git_env git check-ref-format --branch "$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+    || die "invalid worktree branch: $branch"
+  printf '%s' "$branch"
+}
+prepare_lake() { # <worktree> <check-only: 0|1>
+  local tree="$1" check_only="$2" root branch target link actual
+  [ -n "${MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT:-}" ] || return 0
+  [ -d "$tree" ] || die "worktree does not exist: $tree"
+  tree="$(cd "$tree" && pwd -P)"
+  root="$(canonical_lake_root "$((1 - check_only))")"
+  case "$root/" in "$tree/"*) die "the Lake root must be outside the worktree" ;; esac
+  case "$tree/" in "$root/"*) die "the worktree must be outside the Lake root" ;; esac
+  branch="$(worktree_branch "$tree")"
+  target="$root/$branch"
+  link="$tree/.lake"
+  if [ -L "$link" ]; then
+    actual="$(readlink "$link")"
+    [ "$actual" = "$target" ] \
+      || die "$link points to $actual, expected $target; refusing to orphan build data"
+    [ ! -L "$target" ] || die "external Lake target must not be a symlink: $target"
+    if [ "$check_only" -eq 1 ]; then
+      [ -d "$target" ] || die "$link is dangling; expected directory $target"
+    else
+      mkdir -p "$target"
+    fi
+    log "$link already points to $target"
+    return 0
+  fi
+  if [ "$check_only" -eq 1 ]; then
+    die "$link is not a symlink to $target"
+  fi
+  if [ -e "$link" ]; then
+    [ -d "$link" ] || die "$link exists and is not a directory"
+    [ -z "$(find "$link" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] \
+      || die "$link is populated; migrate it explicitly before enabling MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT"
+  fi
+  [ ! -L "$target" ] || die "external Lake target must not be a symlink: $target"
+  if [ -e "$target" ] && [ ! -d "$target" ]; then
+    die "external Lake target exists and is not a directory: $target"
+  fi
+  mkdir -p "$target"
+  [ ! -d "$link" ] || rmdir "$link"
+  ln -s "$target" "$link"
+  log "$link -> $target"
+}
+cleanup_lake() { # <repository> <branch>
+  local repo="$1" branch="$2" root target line listing tree
+  [ -d "$repo" ] || die "repository does not exist: $repo"
+  repo="$(cd "$repo" && pwd -P)"
+  root="$(canonical_lake_root 0)" \
+    || die "MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT must be set for lake-root cleanup"
+  case "$root/" in "$repo/"*) die "the Lake root must be outside the repository" ;; esac
+  case "$repo/" in "$root/"*) die "the repository must be outside the Lake root" ;; esac
+  run_outside_git_env git check-ref-format --branch "$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+    || die "invalid branch name: $branch"
+  target="$root/$branch"

+    || die "cannot read the worktree registry under $repo"

+    ;;

+esac

@@ -0,0 +1,131 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Regression tests for external per-worktree Lake directories."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin"))
+import pr_merge  # noqa: E402
+
+HELPER = REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin" / "lake-root.sh"
+WARMER = REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin" / "warm-worktree.sh"
+HOUSEKEEPING = REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin" / "housekeeping.sh"
+
+
+def run(argv: list[str | Path], *, env: dict[str, str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
+    return subprocess.run(
+        [str(item) for item in argv], cwd=REPO_ROOT, env=env,
+        text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
+    )
+
+
+def git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> None:
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["git", *args], cwd=repo, text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
+    )
+    if result.returncode != 0:
+        raise AssertionError(result.stderr)
+
+
+class LakeRootTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self) -> None:
+        holder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(holder.cleanup)
+        self.tmp = Path(holder.name)
+        self.lake_root = self.tmp / "external-lake"
+        self.env = dict(os.environ, MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT=str(self.lake_root))
+
+    def make_repo(self, name: str, branch: str) -> Path:
+        repo = self.tmp / name
+        repo.mkdir()
+        git(repo, "init", "-q")
+        git(repo, "symbolic-ref", "HEAD", f"refs/heads/{branch}")
+        git(repo, "-c", "user.name=Test", "-c", "user.email=test@example.invalid",
+            "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "seed")
+        return repo
+
+    def test_prepare_places_lake_by_full_branch_and_is_idempotent(self) -> None:
+        repo = self.make_repo("worktree", "codex/issue-test")
+        target = self.lake_root / "codex" / "issue-test"
+        first = run([HELPER, "prepare", repo], env=self.env)
+        second = run([HELPER, "prepare", repo, "--check"], env=self.env)
+        self.assertEqual(first.returncode, 0, first.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(second.returncode, 0, second.stderr)
+        self.assertTrue((repo / ".lake").is_symlink())
+        self.assertEqual(os.readlink(repo / ".lake"), str(target))
+        self.assertTrue(target.is_dir())
+
+    def test_prepare_preserves_populated_lake_and_conflicting_link(self) -> None:
+        populated = self.make_repo("populated", "issue-populated")
+        (populated / ".lake").mkdir()
+        (populated / ".lake" / "keep").write_text("build", encoding="utf-8")
+        result = run([HELPER, "prepare", populated], env=self.env)
+        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
+        self.assertEqual((populated / ".lake" / "keep").read_text(), "build")
+
+        linked = self.make_repo("linked", "issue-linked")
+        other = self.tmp / "other-lake"
+        other.mkdir()
+        (linked / ".lake").symlink_to(other)
+        result = run([HELPER, "prepare", linked], env=self.env)
+        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(os.readlink(linked / ".lake"), str(other))
+
+    def test_warmer_honors_lake_root_without_fetching_or_building(self) -> None:
+        repo = self.make_repo("warm", "issue-warm")
+        for name in ("lean-toolchain", "lake-manifest.json", "lakefile.toml"):
+            (repo / name).write_text(name, encoding="utf-8")
+        fake_bin = self.tmp / "bin"
+        fake_bin.mkdir()
+        fake_lake = fake_bin / "lake"
+        fake_lake.write_text("#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n", encoding="utf-8")
+        fake_lake.chmod(0o755)
+        env = dict(self.env, PATH=f"{fake_bin}:{self.env['PATH']}",
+                   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT=str(self.tmp / "cache"))
+        result = run(
+            [WARMER, repo, "--force-cold", "--skip-packages", "--no-build"], env=env,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(os.readlink(repo / ".lake"),
+                         str(self.lake_root / "issue-warm"))
+
+    def test_cleanup_refuses_active_branch_then_removes_retired_tree(self) -> None:
+        repo = self.make_repo("cleanup-owner", "main")
+        worktree = self.tmp / "cleanup-worktree"
+        git(repo, "branch", "issue-cleanup")
+        git(repo, "worktree", "add", "-q", str(worktree), "issue-cleanup")
+        self.assertEqual(run([HELPER, "prepare", worktree], env=self.env).returncode, 0)
+        target = self.lake_root / "issue-cleanup"
+        (target / "artifact").write_text("generated", encoding="utf-8")
+        active = run([HELPER, "cleanup", repo, "issue-cleanup"], env=self.env)
+        self.assertNotEqual(active.returncode, 0)
+        self.assertTrue(target.is_dir())
+        git(repo, "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(worktree))
+        retired = run([HELPER, "cleanup", repo, "issue-cleanup"], env=self.env)
+        self.assertEqual(retired.returncode, 0, retired.stderr)
+        self.assertFalse(target.exists())
+
+    def test_merge_cleanup_calls_housekeeping_after_worktree_removal(self) -> None:
+        listing = "worktree /tmp/retired\nbranch refs/heads/issue-retired\n"
+        completed = subprocess.CompletedProcess([], 0, "", "removed\n")
+        with mock.patch.object(pr_merge, "git", return_value=listing), \
+                mock.patch.object(pr_merge, "git_ok", side_effect=[True, True]), \
+                mock.patch.object(pr_merge.subprocess, "run", return_value=completed) as cleanup:
+            with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, self.env):
+                pr_merge.remove_branch_and_worktree(REPO_ROOT, "issue-retired")
+        cleanup.assert_called_once_with(
+            [str(HOUSEKEEPING), "lake-cleanup", "issue-retired"], cwd=str(REPO_ROOT),
+            text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+"""Regression tests for external per-worktree Lake directories."""

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import subprocess

+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

+WARMER = REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin" / "warm-worktree.sh"
+HOUSEKEEPING = REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin" / "housekeeping.sh"
+
+def run(argv: list[str | Path], *, env: dict[str, str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
+    return subprocess.run(
+        [str(item) for item in argv], cwd=REPO_ROOT, env=env,
+        text=True, capture_output=True, check=False,
+    )
+
+def git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> None:
+    result = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo, text=True, capture_output=True)
+    if result.returncode != 0:
+        raise AssertionError(result.stderr)
+
+class LakeRootTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self) -> None:
+        holder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(holder.cleanup)
+        self.tmp = Path(holder.name)
+        self.lake_root = self.tmp / "external-lake"
+        self.env = dict(os.environ, MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT=str(self.lake_root))
+
+    def make_repo(self, name: str, branch: str) -> Path:
+        repo = self.tmp / name
+        repo.mkdir()
+        git(repo, "init", "-q")
+        git(repo, "symbolic-ref", "HEAD", f"refs/heads/{branch}")
+        git(repo, "-c", "user.name=Test", "-c", "user.email=test@example.invalid",
+            "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "seed")
+        return repo
+
+    def test_prepare_places_lake_by_full_branch_and_is_idempotent(self) -> None:
+        repo = self.make_repo("worktree", "codex/issue-test")
+        target = self.lake_root / "codex" / "issue-test"
+        first = run([HELPER, "prepare", repo], env=self.env)
+        second = run([HELPER, "prepare", repo, "--check"], env=self.env)
+        self.assertEqual(first.returncode, 0, first.stderr)
+        self.assertEqual(second.returncode, 0, second.stderr)
+        self.assertTrue((repo / ".lake").is_symlink())
+        self.assertEqual(os.readlink(repo / ".lake"), str(target))
+        self.assertTrue(target.is_dir())
+

+

+        other = self.tmp / "other-lake"

+        (linked / ".lake").symlink_to(other)

+        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(os.readlink(linked / ".lake"), str(other))

+

    37	The single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable
    38	cache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the
    39	same failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared
    40	build tree.
    41	
    42	---
    43	
    44	## 2. The two-tier split
    45	
    46	`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and
    47	different sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the
    48	parent's failure.
    49	
    50	The whole per-worktree `.lake` may live on another volume. When the absolute
    51	`MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` is set, `worktree-setup.sh` and `warm-worktree.sh` make
    52	`.lake` an absolute symlink to `$MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT/<branch>`. This changes
    53	placement, not ownership: each branch still has one private writable build tree.
    54	Populated directories and conflicting symlinks are never moved or replaced
    55	implicitly; they require an operator-managed migration.
    56	
    57	**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,
    58	`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the
    59	parent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and
    60	distributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**
    61	copy.
    62	
    63	**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The
    64	parent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud
    65	cache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once
    66	per manifest** in a shared, read-only store:
    67	`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,
    68	and every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.
    69	
    70	> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a
    71	> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it
    72	> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any
    73	> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest
    74	> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by
    75	> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old
    76	> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches
    77	> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,
    78	> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key
    79	> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).
    80	> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.
    81	
    82	Consequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It
    83	rewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under
    84	every published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib

    88	
    89	## 3. The cache key
    90	
    91	```
    92	keyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )
    93	```

   450	* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked

   463	## 10. Operating procedures
   464	
   465	```bash
   466	# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).
   467	local/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main
   468	
   469	# What is published right now?
   470	local/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status
   471	
   472	# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.
   473	MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT=/fast/lake local/bin/worktree-setup.sh \

   475

   477	MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT=/fast/lake local/bin/housekeeping.sh \

   479

   481	local/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check
   482	
   483	# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.
   484	local/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force
   485	
   486	# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?
   487	local/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status
   488	```
   489	
   490	After a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm
   491	first, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot
   492	is invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run

   499	
   500	| condition | behaviour |
   501	|---|---|
   502	| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |
   503	| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |

   262	## 8. Concurrency
   263	
   264	- **One writing session per worktree.** `dispatch.sh` takes a lock named after
   265	  the worktree for the whole run of any non-`read-only` session and fails fast
   266	  (exit 5) if another dispatch holds it; `--lock-wait SECONDS` queues instead.
   267	  Read-only sessions are never blocked. Parallel work means parallel
   268	  worktrees, not parallel sessions in one worktree.
   269	- **Locks live in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/`**, never in the repository,
   270	  and are `mkdir`-based (macOS has no `flock(1)`). A lock whose owning pid is
   271	  gone is broken automatically, with a notice.
   272	- **Telemetry appends are locked** inside `telemetry.py`, so concurrent
   273	  sessions cannot interleave a half-written JSON line.
   274	- Do not defend against collisions with a single global lock. The parent
   275	  repository learned this the expensive way: a workflow-level concurrency
   276	  group let an unrelated event cancel an in-progress fix, and the fix was to
   277	  scope the group correctly rather than to widen it (`auto-fix.yml:29-32`).
   278	- The build lock is a separate mechanism: one full `lake build` machine-wide
   279	  at a time (`DESIGN.md` invariant 7, `build-cache.md`). A dispatched session
   280	  inherits that discipline; it does not get its own exemption.

   216	   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.

   223	### 5.3 Atomic publish
   224	
   225	The publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:
   226	
   227	1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with
   228	   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the
   229	   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).
   230	2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.
   231	3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.
   232	   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already
   233	   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**
   234	4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over
   235	   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).

   238	> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would
   239	> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real
   240	> trap, not a hypothetical one.

   299	  clone;

   301	  alone and warn. It may hold hours of an agent's incremental work; replacing it
   302	  with a main snapshot is destructive and is only done under `--force`.
   303	
   304	### 6.2 Why copy-on-write, and why not a symlink
   305	
   306	On APFS, `cp -c -R` clones extents rather than bytes: the operation is near
   307	instantaneous and initially consumes no additional space, with divergence paid
   308	for only as the worktree's own build writes new blocks. This is what makes a
   309	*private writable copy per worktree* affordable — and a private writable copy is
   310	precisely what preserves the single-writer invariant. A writable symlink or
   311	bind-style share of `.lake/build` across two concurrent `lake build` invocations
   312	is the local restatement of the parent's eviction bug and is never acceptable.

item.text:
## Findings

- [ ] F5 (blocker) `local/bin/lake-root.sh:17` — The one-way hot-cache check permits a Lake target containing `hot-main`, which cleanup then recursively deletes.
- [ ] F6 (blocker) `local/bin/lake-root.sh:33` — In-root symlink aliases can make two branches share one target, allowing cleanup to delete an active worktree’s build tree.
- [ ] F7 (changes) `local/bin/pr_merge.py:435` — Cleanup silently skips external products when the environment variable is absent or the worktree was already removed.
- [ ] F8 (changes) `local/bin/lake-root.sh:51` — Preparation accepts roots inside another checkout that cleanup subsequently refuses.

## Review

F5: `reject_hot_main` checks only whether its argument is equal to or below a protected path. With `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT=$MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT/<branch>`, the branch target contains `hot-main` and passes validation; line 106 then removes the entire cache root. A temporary reproduction confirmed deletion of the protected cache tree. The overlap check must also reject targets that contain protected paths.

F6: `validated_target` accepts canonical targets anywhere below the root. Given `root/a -> root/b`, branches `a/x` and `b/x` resolve to the same directory. Cleanup compares raw link strings at line 97, misses the active alias, and removes its canonical directory. A temporary reproduction left the active worktree with a dangling `.lake`. Reject symlinked branch-path components or enforce canonical target uniqueness.

F7: The cleanup call is nested under both `if target` and an ambient `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT`. Setup and merge are separate invocations, so that environment is not durable; retries after worktree removal also make zero cleanup calls. Capture or persist the validated association and invoke cleanup independently of worktree discovery, with a loud warning when it cannot be recovered.

F8: For a linked worktree, preparation compares the root only with that checkout. A root inside the primary checkout is accepted and populated, but cleanup rejects it against the primary repository at lines 85–86. Validate against the common repository and registered worktrees before creating anything.

Prior F1–F4 are resolved as originally stated: root aliases are canonicalized before the `/` guard, outside-root symlink escapes are rejected, descendants of `hot-main` are rejected, and writable dispatches receive the resolved target via `--add-dir`.

Verification: all 15 focused tests passed; `git diff --check` and shell syntax checks passed. `shellcheck` was unavailable. The worktree remained clean.
